title: Projection-density shrinking for an open in a smooth square
statement: Let $B$ be a field or a discrete valuation ring [def-weil-field, def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], put $S=\operatorname{Spec}B$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and let $X\to S$ be smooth, separated and of finite type [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Products and fibres are scheme-theoretic base changes [def-pc-base-change]. Let $Z\subseteq P=X\times_SX$ be open [def-weil-open-immersion], and suppose $Z_s$ is dense in $P_s$ for every $s\in S$. There is a smooth separated finite-type open subscheme $A\subseteq X$, with $A_s$ dense in $X_s$ for every $s\in S$, such that for every $a\in A$ both $Z\times_{X,p_1|_Z}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(a)$ and $Z\times_{X,p_2|_Z}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(a)$ are dense in the respective fibres of $p_1,p_2:P\to X$ [def-weil-residue-field]. In particular $Z\cap(A\times_SA)$ is dense in every fibre of both projections $A\times_SA\to A$. If $B$ is a discrete valuation ring with fraction field $F$ and $Z_F=P_F$, one can choose $A$ to contain $X_F$. No multiplication on $X$ is part of the data.

source.place: BLR 5.2 Proposition 2, proof, construction of T_1,T_2 and Omega_1,Omega_2 before defining U prime, printed pp.115-116 (PDF pp.121-122); uses 2.5 Lemma 1(a); primary scan read at https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~kamenova/homepage_files/Bosch_Raynaud_Neron_Model_tc.pdf; local literature copy WANTED.

proof.text: The base $S$ is Noetherian: a field has only two ideals, while a discrete valuation ring is a principal ideal ring. Thus $X$ is Noetherian by the finite-type theorem. Each $p_i:P\to X$ is a smooth base change of $X\to S$, and is of finite presentation: smoothness gives local finite presentation; finite type gives quasi-compactness; separatedness gives quasi-separatedness since its diagonal is a closed immersion, whose inverse images of affine opens are affine. The quasi-compact and quasi-separated conditions are preserved by base change. The scheme $P$ and all fibres in use are Noetherian by finite type and base change.

source.place: BLR 5.2 Proposition 2, proof, printed pp.115-116 (PDF pp.121-122), construction of the two bad loci and their closure complements; primary scan inspected online; local copy WANTED.

proof.text: Put $C=|P|\setminus|Z|$. Apply the smooth closed-fibre codimension-locus theorem to each $p_i$, with closed subset $C$ and $c=1$. Its constructible set $G_{i,1}$ consists exactly of parameters whose fibre of $C$ contains no irreducible component. Equivalently $Z_a$ is dense in $(P,p_i)_a$: an open is dense precisely when it contains every component generic point. Indeed a dense open contains such a generic point because a neighbourhood meeting only that component can be obtained by removing the other finitely many components; conversely containing the generic points makes its closure contain every component. Consequently $T_i=X\setminus G_{i,1}$ is constructible, and it is exactly the set of bad parameters for $p_i$.

source.place: BLR 5.2 Proposition 2, proof, printed pp.115-116 (PDF pp.121-122), construction of the two bad loci and their closure complements; primary scan inspected online; local copy WANTED.

proof.text: For the fibre inclusion $X_s\to X$, the residue-field formula reduces to $\kappa(x)\otimes_{\kappa(s)}\kappa(s)=\kappa(x)$. Thus the residue fields agree, and iterated base change identifies the projection fibre calculated in $P_s\to X_s$ with that in $P\to X$. Fix $s\in S$ and a component generic point $\xi$ of $X_s$. Every component generic point $y$ of the $p_i$-fibre above $\xi$ is a component generic point of $P_s$. To check this without any identification of scheme products with topological products, use the fibre homeomorphism. A generalization of $y$ in $P_s$ maps to a generalization of $\xi$, hence maps to $\xi$ itself; in that fibre, $y$ has no proper generalization. Thus $y$ has no proper generalization in $P_s$, as required. Density and openness of $Z_s$ put all these generic points in $Z_s$ by the preceding finite-component criterion. That criterion in the projection fibre now proves $\xi\notin T_i$. This applies also to empty projection fibres. In particular every component generic point of either base fibre is good for both projections.

proof.text: For a field base, every generalization of a component generic point of $X$ equals that point, hence is good by step 3. For a DVR base, the generic fibre $X_F=D(\pi)$ is open, so a component generic point in it also has no proper generalization in $X$. At a component generic point $\xi$ of the special fibre, the local-ring assertion of the smooth-trait spreading lemma gives $\mathcal O_{X,\xi}$ a DVR structure. Its canonical spectrum map has image all generalizations of $\xi$. A DVR has exactly its zero and maximal primes: every nonzero prime ideal, being principal with nonzero generator $u\varpi^n$, contains the uniformizer. The spectrum therefore has two points, with distinct images in $X$: the canonical map induces local-ring isomorphisms, whereas one source local ring is a field and the other is a nonfield DVR. Besides $\xi$ there is exactly one generalization $\gamma$; it has no proper generalization and lies over the generic point of $S$ (otherwise it would contradict genericity of $\xi$ in $X_k$). Thus $\gamma$ is a component generic point of $X_F$. Both $\xi$ and $\gamma$ are good by step 3. We have proved that every generalization of every fibre component generic point is outside $T_i$.

source.place: BLR 5.2 Proposition 2, proof, printed pp.115-116 (PDF pp.121-122), construction of the two bad loci and their closure complements; primary scan inspected online; local copy WANTED.

proof.text: Set $H_i=\overline{T_i}$ in $X$. No fibre component generic point $\xi$ belongs to $H_i$. Here is the closure argument, which is needed because closure need not commute with passage to a fibre. Write the constructible $T_i$ as a finite union $\bigcup_j(U_j\cap F_j)$, with $U_j$ open and $F_j$ closed. If $\xi\in H_i$, it belongs to $\overline{U_j\cap F_j}$ for some $j$. Decompose $F_j$ into its finitely many irreducible components. For a component $E$, the intersection $U_j\cap E$ is either empty or dense in $E$. Thus $\overline{U_j\cap F_j}$ is precisely the union of the components $E$ which meet $U_j$. One of these $E$ contains $\xi$. Its generic point $e$ lies in $U_j\cap F_j\subset T_i$, and $e$ generalizes $\xi$. This contradicts step 4. Hence $H_i$ avoids every component generic point in every fibre.

source.place: Tag 005K, lemma-generic-point-in-constructible, finite locally closed decomposition; the closure argument is written out using Noetherian finite components.

proof.text: Define $A=X\setminus(H_1\cup H_2)$. It is open. In every fibre it contains all component generic points by step 5, so $A_s$ is dense in $X_s$ by the finite-component criterion. The restriction $A\to S$ is smooth by the open-immersion smooth-composition theorem. It is separated: its diagonal is the restriction of the closed diagonal of $X\to S$ to $A\times_S A$. It is of finite type: opens of a Noetherian scheme are quasi-compact; indeed an ascending-open maximality argument turns any open covering into a finite subcover. Every inverse image in $A$ of an affine open of $X$ is open in the Noetherian scheme $A$, hence quasi-compact. Locally, an open immersion is covered by basic localizations $R\to R_f$, generated by $f^{-1}$, hence is locally of finite type. Compose with $X\to S$. This includes $X=\varnothing$ and fibres which are empty.

source.place: BLR 5.2 Proposition 2, proof, printed pp.115-116 (PDF pp.121-122), construction of the two bad loci and their closure complements; primary scan inspected online; local copy WANTED.

proof.text: For $a\in A$ we have $a\notin T_i\subset H_i$ for both $i$. By the definition of $T_i$ this gives the two asserted densities in the full $p_i$-fibres $X_{\kappa(a)}$. The fibre of $A\times_S A\to A$ above $a$ is the open subscheme $A_{\kappa(a)}$ of that full fibre. A dense subset meets every nonempty open, so restricting the dense open $Z_a$ to this open fibre leaves a dense subset of the open fibre. This proves the density assertion for $Z\cap(A\times_S A)$ for both projections.

source.place: BLR 5.2 Proposition 2, proof, printed pp.115-116 (PDF pp.121-122), construction of the two bad loci and their closure complements; primary scan inspected online; local copy WANTED.

proof.text: Finally suppose $B$ is a DVR and $Z_F=P_F$. Every parameter in $X_F$ is then good, so $T_i\subset X_k$ for both $i$. The special fibre is closed: it is the inverse image of the vanishing set of the uniformizer. Therefore $H_i=\overline{T_i}\subset X_k$. The very same $A$ consequently contains all of $X_F$, proving the additional clause without modifying the construction.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-N9-eb3e176aa (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Statement is byte-identical to live (first split, no proof before, no new nodes, no cycle in the 429-node closure). BLR 5.2 Prop 2 has no local copy and the proof is by:agent and self-contained, so I checked each step against the cited statements and the BLR route. S1 smooth (proper-base-change (2)), qcqs and finite-presentation projections over a Noetherian X. S2 the last clause of the smooth-closed-fibre-codimension-locus lemma (c=1, C=P\Z) gives exactly the parameters whose fibre is good; the bad locus T_i is constructible by closure under complements. S3 a generic point of a projection fibre over a component generic point of X_s has no proper generalization in P_s, so it lies in Z_s; checked by sobriety. S4 O_{X,xi} is a DVR by the unconditional local-ring clause of the smooth-trait spreading lemma (instantiated with identities). Its two primes map to xi and to one generic point of X_F; X_F=D(pi) is open. S5 is the closure argument of 005K, written out from the finite locally closed decomposition and correct. S6 smooth, separated and finite-type open; S7 density restricts to the open fibre A_{kappa(a)}; S8 T_i lies in the closed X_k, so A contains X_F. Small cases checked: X empty, field base, A^1 over a DVR with Z=P\V(pi,x_1) (shrinking really needed), mixed-dimension fibres. No duplicate found (rg -L over dag/nodes). Batch-5: lem-trf-generic-fibre-dimension-neighborhood (Stacks 05F7) and lem-trf-flat-module-torsionfree-domain (flat implies torsion-free over a domain) are generic algebra. They are not part of the trace formula or Poincare duality and neither assumption gives them, so they are accepted. tool_uses are generic foundations, accepted. No changes.
